content:
Jenna: Heads-up — I'm trying to wire up KMS grants for the new IRSA role used by token-proxy. Terraform plan shows the aws_kms_grant being created, but the pod still gets AccessDenied on Decrypt. Anyone seen this?

Marc: Quick questions: is the grant actually targeting the role ARN (not the web-identity session)? and does the account that runs Terraform have kms:CreateGrant on the key?

Jenna: We're using the role ARN from the aws_iam_role.irsa_role resource as grantee_principal. Provider runs from CI using our infra service account (has full KMS perms AFAIK). Key policy is the default one from aws_kms_key (not edited). Error from the app: "AccessDeniedException: User: arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/IRSA-role/session is not authorized to perform: kms:Decrypt"

Aisha: Common gotchas:
- KMS grants are applied to the principal that does the Decrypt call (the session principal), but Terraform creates a grant using the role ARN — that's okay.
- The critical parts: the KMS key policy must allow the identity that creates grants (Terraform's principal) to call kms:CreateGrant, and it must allow the principal (IRSA role) to use the key — either via key policy or via a grant.

Robin: Also make sure the IRSA role trust policy matches the service account sub exactly. If the role can be assumed, the runtime principal will look like arn:aws:sts::123456789012:assumed-role/<role-name>/<session-name>. Key policy condition examples sometimes break when sub doesn't match.

Marc: Paste of the terraform bits that usually work for us:
```hcl
resource "aws_iam_role" "irsa_role" {
  name = "irsa-token-proxy"
  assume_role_policy = data.aws_iam_policy_document.irsa_trust.json
}

data "aws_iam_policy_document" "irsa_trust" {
  statement {
    actions = ["sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity"]
    principals { type = "Federated"; identifiers = [aws_iam_openid_connect_provider.eks.arn] }
    condition { test = "StringEquals"; variable = "oidc.eks.amazonaws.com:sub"; values = ["system:serviceaccount:platform:token-proxy"] }
  }
}

resource "aws_kms_key" "token" {
  description = "Key for token-proxy"
  deletion_window_in_days = 30
}

resource "aws_kms_grant" "token_decrypt" {
  name              = "token-proxy-decrypt"
  key_id            = aws_kms_key.token.key_id
  grantee_principal = aws_iam_role.irsa_role.arn
  operations        = ["Decrypt", "GenerateDataKey"]
  depends_on        = [aws_iam_role.irsa_role]
}
```

Aisha: Couple more checks: 
- Does the key policy explicitly prevent IAM principals from using the key? If you used the default policy it often only allows the account root and services; adding the role to the key policy is safer than relying on grants that could be rejected if CreateGrant is not allowed.
- Ensure Terraform actually creates the grant after the role exists — sometimes plan shows it but apply ordering can race; depends_on on the role should fix it.

devops: infra-bot ran an automated check on the key policy: it currently has a block limiting "Principal" to "AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:root" and a separate statement for our kms admin service, but not the irsa role. That explains why the grant feels inert.

Jenna: Ahhh. So two options: add the role ARN to the key policy or make sure TF's principal (CI user) can call CreateGrant and the key policy allows CreateGrant. Which do we prefer?

Marc: For long-lived service roles we usually add the role ARN to the key policy with a condition on aws:PrincipalArn to be safe. Grants are better for short-lived cross-account access. Example key policy snippet that worked for us:
```json
{
  "Sid": "AllowIRSAroleUsage",
  "Effect": "Allow",
  "Principal": {"AWS": "arn:aws:iam::123456789012:role/irsa-token-proxy"},
  "Action": ["kms:Decrypt","kms:GenerateDataKey"],
  "Resource": "*"
}
```

Aisha: And ensure you don't accidentally lock out CreateGrant. If you want Terraform to keep managing the grant resource, the key policy must allow the TF principal to call kms:CreateGrant and kms:ListGrants/kms:RetireGrant as appropriate. Otherwise CreateGrant fails at apply time.

Robin: Another small thing: our EKS OIDC provider uses subject format "system:serviceaccount:<ns>:<sa>" — if the sub in role trust doesn't match the SA name exactly (including namespace), the pod will be able to assume role? No, it will fail. Double-check that.

Jenna: I'll patch the key policy to include the role ARN and re-run apply. Also add depends_on on the iam role for the grant resource. If that still fails, I'll switch to key-policy-only (no grant).

devops: FYI I dropped a link to our internal KMS patterns doc in #docs: https://internal.redwood/kms-patterns (private). It has a terraform module snippet we use for service roles.

Marc: If you want, I can review the policy change once you push a branch. Also consider attaching a resource-based policy to the role (inline) that documents why the role exists — helps audits.

Jenna: Thanks all. Pushing a small PR now, tagging @Marc and @Aisha for review.

infra-bot: CI started for branch jenna/tf-kms-irsa-fix — terraform plan in progress :gear:

Robin: :thumbsup: Let us know if plan shows any denied actions.
